doc.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001

title: Great musicians who did not read well
summary: Brubeck argues that musicians without formal skills can contribute hugely, citing Ellington, Armstrong, Garner, Tatum and Shearing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Oh that’s just gorgeous. Do you find that in gaining more knowledge about how things work, is it restrictive at all for you? Because you have said that it’s good to be an innocent.

I have not got the capability to study like other guys. It has to be by osmosis or just some other way. And there’s plenty of my friends that work that way that have turned out great music that don’t read well and haven’t studied a lot but write so beautifully. And there might be something to acknowledge that if a person doesn’t have the usual skills, don’t count him out. He might have something else going on that is/are unusual because they aren’t the usual. And in my experience some of my favorite musicians didn’t have

reading skills or orchestrating skills, had to pick it up in their own way and have contributed maybe more than anybody else. So there’s something — I’ll tell you Ellington wasn’t the greatest reader, did you know that?

Yeah. Neither was Louis Armstrong. And Garner, who is one of my favorites, was — he didn’t know about reading, didn’t need to know and didn’t care. So how did he develop you know. He was perfection. And Art Tatum — there’s never been anybody yet with his ability, and yet he was a person that didn’t read, he just heard and produced and wrote — not wrote, he played. And he had command of the harmonic and rhythmic ideas more than anybody I’ve ever known. And there’s people like George Shearing that, it’s amazing, he’s learned through rote and through Braille and combined everything. That’s one of the most amazing guys I know is Shearing. The way he refuses to be in any way defeated. He’s more organized than most people I’ve ever known.
